CHEMISTRY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Chemistry? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Chemistry.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Chemistry.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Chemistry.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Chemistry.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2.? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Acids and Bases 2..

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Milk souring

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Atom? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Atom.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Atom.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Atom.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Atom.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat.

6. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

7. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size.

9. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

10. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

11. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Acids and bases? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Acids and bases.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Acids and bases.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids and bases.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Acids and bases.

13. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

14. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

15. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Producers
   D. Decomposers only

16. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only carbon dioxide

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Periodic Table ● Development of the periodic table . ● Ion formation . ● For.

18. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys.

19. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Acids and Bases 2.2. Introduction to Salts 3.0 Organic Chemistry Page 15 of 40 1.

20. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Salts ● Types of salts ● solubility of salts (chlorides, carbona and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Chemistry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain The Atom 1.3. The periodic Table 1.4. Chemical Bonding 1.5. Periodicity 2.0 Phys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Chemical Bonding ● valence electron in bonding ● bond type (ionic, covalent, dat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Periodicity ● Trends in groups I, II, VII, VIII and period 3 ● gradation in size and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
